最荒谬的是，不管你的Agent最终帮你砍下多少钱，也不管商家的Agent多榨出了多少溢价，这中间高频博弈烧掉的庞大算力，最后全都会变成打给云巨头和老黄的通道费。相当于买卖双方在盘口厮杀得头破血流，最后全去给交易所交了算力印花税

$SPY
 收报778.10，跌0.06%；以科网股为主的纳指ETF QQQ 失守750关，收报746.04，跌0.70%，为三大指数中最弱；道指ETF DIA 则逆市造好，收报517.91，升0.35%；罗素2000小型股ETF IWM 反复偏软，收报277.88，跌0.38%。指数跌幅虽浅，市宽却明显转弱——104只观察股中仅29只收升、75只下跌，跌者为升者逾两倍半，显示大市全日由少数权重股顶住，并非普涨。

**板块**
防守及旧经济板块逆市靠稳。能源股造好，XOM 升1.90%、OXY 升1.70%、CVX 升1.42%；必需消费 WMT 升1.55%、COST 升1.32%。大型科网股内部亦见分化，META 升3.38%为权重股之首，AAPL 升1.29%，软件股 CRM 升2.09%。另一边，半导体与光通讯一线全日急泻，是拖低纳指的主因；三倍反向半导体ETF SOXS 单日升8.14%，为全日升幅之冠，SQQQ 升2.06%，反映资金明显转向对冲科技仓位。

**焦点**
跌幅榜由光通讯及光学一线主导：SMTC 挫10.15%、CIEN 泻9.95%、LITE 跌9.78%、AAOI 跌8.17%、COHR 跌7.87%，半导体设备 AEHR 跌7.63%，互联芯片 CRDO 跌7.25%，玻璃及光纤 GLW 跌6.00%；此外燃料电池 BE 跌6.50%，量子计算概念 IONQ 泻9.07%，同列跌幅前段。值得注意的是，此一板块的走势与市场仍在热炒的AI数据中心、电力主题方向相反：整条AI供应链多数环节由美国、台湾、韩国掐住中国，光模块这一层却是少数反过来的，美国同业的估值溢价因此最先承压。产业消息方面，市场续传亚马逊正商讨以约70亿美元收购AI初创Decart，而Anthropic早前议价至60亿美元、完成尽调后放弃，差价背后是AWS自研Trainium芯片生态不足的补课成本。同属卡位讨论的还有EUV环节——真正无可替代的并非 ASML ，而是独家供应EUV反射镜的德国蔡司，其母体为不设股东、不上市的基金会，外界无从投资。

**小结**
全日格局为「指数窄幅、内部剧震」：资金自AI硬件最贵的一端撤出，转入能源、必需消费及少数大型科网，道指得以逆市收升，纳指则独自受压。分析指，QQQ 失守750关为短线首个警号，若市宽维持29升75跌的极端分化，指数层面的平稳未必持续；光通讯一线的沽压是否见底，仍需观察 CIEN 、LITE 等能否先行收复本日跌幅。

People don't quite realize this, but I've turned down 50+ companies that offered me a partnership.

So when 
@liquidtrading
 offered one, I did what I'd done with every company before them. I listened, and I kindly said no.

But like I do with stocks, I took more time and did a deep dive. I wanted to understand the story behind it, and why so many people in my Discord were already using the product.

Then I used it myself, for my own trading, and got to meet the management team and hear their story and their drive.

As a product person, I love trying a product that puts the user's needs first and is transparent. Liquid is upfront about its fees and the risks of leverage, the platform is incredibly easy to use, and the team moves fast on fixing bugs and improving the product.

What actually won me over is that I like using leverage but hate decay. I already run some margin on my account, but I don't like call options. Taking on more leverage at a known cost, instead of fighting time decay, feels like an easier trade to take.

Like everything in life, I'm approaching this with caution. I don't think everyone should use leverage, and I don't think anyone, myself included, should trade large amounts of money on Liquid. I've set a limit on how much I'll move here from my long portfolio.

This is my weekend fun, and boy, I don't remember the last time I had this much fun trading. It's not because I'm up 350% with a 90% win rate, although that sure has given me a rush. The real winner is the social side, the transparency and the gamification of the platform.

My subs and I are running a tournament. We look out for each other and sit out when conditions are bad. Even after such a mixed week, no one has lost money. That doesn't mean they can't, but we've gotten more in tune with trading the news and being in the moment.

This is certainly not for everyone. But for me, it's such a relief to trade a smaller portfolio, to test my skills against the very best of FinX and to have fun doing so.

Not all neoclouds are created the same way not all neocloud capacity is worth the same, and this chart shows it.

Every gigawatt Nebius signs away in a long-term hosting deal brings in roughly $20-25B. 

The same gigawatt sold short-term on its own platform brings in $40-50B. Same power, same data center, about double the revenue.

Serverless inference is the purest version of that.

$NBIS
:

+ Usage-based pricing scales with adoption. More agents means more tokens, which means more revenue from the same gigawatt.
+ The software is the moat. Uptime guarantees, speculative decoding and auto-scaling are hard to copy for someone who's just renting out racks.
+ It spreads revenue across thousands of customers instead of a couple of hyperscalers.

The big contracts pay for the build but inference is where the money is.

Bet on the companies that are pushing for more server-less inference.

$NBIS


Bloomberg Intelligence just modeled return on invested capital (ROIC) through 2030 for the clouds and neoclouds, and the 
$NBIS
 line is the one I keep staring at.

Nebius goes from roughly −6% in 2026 to about 9% by 2030. That’s the steepest climb of any neocloud in the model, and it passes CoreWeave around 2029. AWS goes the other way, sliding from ~24% to ~16% as AI depreciation piles up.

Yes, the neoclouds are still below their cost of capital in BI’s numbers. 

That’s what a buildout looks like early on: you pour the concrete and buy the GPUs first, and the returns show up after.

Nebius writes its GPUs off over 4 years, faster than CoreWeave’s 6. Meanwhile the H100 is almost four years old and still rents near 2025 prices. As Nebius’s first H100s roll off that 4-year schedule, they can keep renting with almost nothing left to depreciate, and that drops straight into margin. 

Fully written-off GPUs also shrink the capital base, so ROIC gets a lift from both sides.

If GPUs keep earning that long, the depreciation drag shrinks and that 9% moves up fast.

Bullish, but not all Neoclouds are created equal.
